reference_opening.argument: This video is non-scam content because it is a promotional interview about BitClub Network, financial education, cryptocurrency mining and sharing information with the speaker's team. The speakers express positive expectations, including that the future will be safe and profitable and that others can receive similar opportunities, but the supplied content does not show a payment request, a specific paid mining package, a tiered earnings structure or a sensitive-data request. The observed activity is therefore business promotion without enough concrete evidence in this video to classify it as a deceptive solicitation.

citations.quote: BICLUB is one of the motorbikes that has helped me to realize where economy has gone
We are going to see a future where it's safe and profitable.
I want to help so that others will get the same opportunities like I have.
I'd like to share information with my team.

opening.argument: The video links participation in BitClub's mining business to unusually favorable outcomes. The speaker says he entered cryptocurrency, then “opened my eyes to the world of mining,” and that this business “has provided me a lot.” Another speaker describes BitClub as providing opportunities and predicts a future that is “safe and profitable.” The practical invitation is to join the information flow: the speaker wants to share what he learned with “my team,” while the video visibly supplies a contact address. Read together, this is not merely abstract education; it presents mining involvement as the action through which viewers can obtain substantial benefits. The missing package price or payment instruction does not undo the implied solicitation, because the promised benefit is attached to entering and participating in the mining business.

citations.quote: I have been in the world of cryptocurrency for a year and a half and three months ago I opened my eyes to the world of mining.
I have been in this business since June and the truth is that it has provided me a lot
We are going to see a future where it's safe and profitable.
I'd like to share information with my team.

rebuttal.rebuttal: The defense treats the absence of a stated price or package as decisive, but the promotional message does not need to spell out every transaction step to create a solicitation. It repeatedly connects BitClub, cryptocurrency mining, personal benefit and a safe, profitable future. Calling this “financial education” describes the framing, not what viewers are being encouraged to pursue. The visible contact information and team-oriented sharing also give the positive mining claims a participation pathway, even if the video leaves the exact commercial terms unstated.

citations.quote: One of the pillars that BICLUB has given me is mainly financial education.
We are going to see a future where it's safe and profitable.
I'd like to share information with my team.

true_side_reply.rebuttal: The quotes establish enthusiasm, not paid mining returns. “Opened my eyes to the world of mining” and “provided me a lot” do not say that the speaker bought hashpower, purchased a mining package, or receives recurring income. “Safe and profitable” is a general forecast, not a promised mining payout tied to a purchase. The visible contact detail likewise does not establish what viewers must buy or what return they would receive, so the evidence supports promotion but not the specific paid-mining mechanism.

citations.quote: I have been in the world of cryptocurrency for a year and a half and three months ago I opened my eyes to the world of mining.
I have been in this business since June and the truth is that it has provided me a lot
We are going to see a future where it's safe and profitable.

opening.argument: Several risk signals appear together rather than in isolation: cryptocurrency, mining, personal testimonial, and an optimistic profitability claim. The speaker presents himself as someone who entered mining recently, reports that the business has “provided me a lot,” and says the future will be “safe and profitable.” That combination gives viewers a success narrative without any displayed explanation of how mining generates the benefit, what conditions apply, or what risks exist. The interview setting and on-screen contact address reinforce that this is an outward-facing promotion. A judge should treat the confident return-oriented framing around an opaque crypto-mining opportunity as deceptive solicitation, even though the short clip does not disclose every operational detail.

citations.quote: I have been in the world of cryptocurrency for a year and a half and three months ago I opened my eyes to the world of mining.
I have been in this business since June and the truth is that it has provided me a lot
We are going to see a future where it's safe and profitable.

rebuttal.rebuttal: The defense calls the clip ordinary business promotion, but that understates the convergence of its signals. This is a first-person endorsement of cryptocurrency mining that emphasizes personal benefit and a safe, profitable future, while offering contact information. No balancing discussion of losses, uncertainty or operating conditions appears in the supplied material. The upbeat testimonial is therefore not neutral education; it is the risk-bearing opportunity being presented in its most attractive light.

citations.quote: I have been in this business since June and the truth is that it has provided me a lot
We are going to see a future where it's safe and profitable.

true_side_reply.rebuttal: Crypto and mining terminology alone is not a scam mechanism. The speaker never states a return rate, recurring payout, package, equipment share, purchase requirement or loss guarantee. The statement that the business “provided me a lot” is vague and could refer to learning or experience; it does not establish income. Likewise, a contact address is evidence of outreach, not evidence that viewers are asked to pay for mining or that any promised return is deceptive.

BitClub Training in Marbella - Sept. 2018 Interview with Unai Martínez (Basque Country) and Dragos Dumitru (Madrid - Romania)

opening.argument: Although the speakers use the language of education and information sharing, the format functions as an endorsement designed to recruit participation. BitClub is named as a source of financial education, one speaker says it helped him understand where the economy has gone, and another says he wants others to receive the same opportunities. The speaker then describes sharing what he learned with his team. That progression turns an apparently educational interview into advocacy for joining an organized opportunity, with personal success and future profitability used to motivate others. The team language is especially significant: it suggests the audience is being positioned as prospective participants in the speaker's network, not merely students receiving neutral financial information.

citations.quote: BitClub Network Marbella - Unai and Dragos
One of the pillars that BICLUB has given me is mainly financial education.
I want to help so that others will get the same opportunities like I have.
I'd like to share information with my team.

rebuttal.rebuttal: The defense's label of “promotional interview” actually supports the concern: the clip is not detached reporting but favorable advocacy. The speakers present BitClub as the source of education, opportunities and profitability, then discuss sharing the message with a team. That is a recruitment-oriented social structure, even if the short excerpt does not enumerate its levels. The absence of an explicit commission table should not conceal the persuasive function of the testimonial.

citations.quote: One of the pillars that BICLUB has given me is mainly financial education.
I want to help so that others will get the same opportunities like I have.
I'd like to share information with my team.

true_side_reply.rebuttal: Promotion does not equal recruitment commissions or a tiered matrix. The speaker says he wants to share information with his team, but never says team members generate his income, join under him, pay him, or qualify him for rewards. “Others will get the same opportunities” is an endorsement, not proof of downlines or commissions. The evidence can show favorable business promotion while failing to establish the specific recruitment mechanism required here.
